title: Open Championship 2026: Matt Fitzpatrick, Jordan Spieth lead big names missing the cut
content:
SOUTHPORT, England — Matt Fitzpatrick cut a frustrated figure as he topped the list of high-profile casualties heading home early from The Open Championship.

As one of the pre-tournament favourites, the 31-year-old Englishman was expected to shine back in the UK, but he blew up in the heat at Royal Birkdale and finished three shots below the cutline after dropping to 4-over on Friday.

Fitzpatrick trailed the second-round leader Lucas Herbert by 12 shots, alongside plenty of other notable names who failed to impress.

The top 70 players, counting ties, make the cut at The Open, which this year ended up being 1-over-par.

Jordan Spieth, the winner from 2017, failed to find any spark on a course he previously ripped to pieces and will also leave early. His putting let him down badly, including a three-putt double bogey from 4 feet at the par-3 seventh. A quadruple-bogey on the par-5 17th dropped him all the way to 10-over.

The previously in-form Wyndham Clark recovered four shots in the closing four holes yet still finished two behind the line after an erratic front nine on Friday. Clark, who won the U.S. Open last month, recorded back-to-back double-bogeys on Nos. 2 and 3, and was up against it from there. Even an early morning tee time, with mild temperatures and lighter winds, offered little advantage.

With the PGA Championship winner, Aaron Rai, also coming up short at 2-over, it means the last two major winners will miss the weekend, and for those sitting out of the next two days, the eight-month countdown to Augusta and the 2027 Masters now begins.

More bruising, though, will be the feeling of missing out as the opportunity to shoot a low score went to waste.

In the calm conditions, Royal Birkdale was there for the taking. Herbert and Sam Burns showed as much with second-round 62s to equal the lowest ever score in The Open, while a stack of other players finished under par.

Henrik Stenson appeared to be in the groove and looked to be rolling back the years on Thursday, but his 68 was wiped out by a 74 in the second, leaving a strong Swedish following disappointed.

Justin Rose also threatened a late comeback, but a bogey on No 12 was damaging, and he failed to recover.

Among other notable golfers to miss the cut were 2023 Open Champion Brian Harman and the runner-up that year, Jason Day, as well as Victor Hovland. Tom Kim also failed to take any momentum from his win at the Genesis Scottish Open into this week.

Elsewhere, Brooks Koepka (+1) and Xander Schauffele (E) squeezed in, but like Rory McIlroy (-1), they’ve all got a lot of work to do if they want to get anywhere near Herbert at the top.
